findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several pans on a shelf being stored as clean were observed soiled with remaining food debris and stickers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. They moved the items back to dish for re-cleaning. Reviewing of procedures and oversight of the dish cleaners is suggested to prevent future issues. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage and re-use in the facility.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler to the left of the fryers was observed holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 48.5F. Due to the situation with the fryers and per the PIC this cooler is not likely to have been opened much since that situation kicked off two days ago. At this time the TCS foods are being discarded due to the situation taking place with the fryers. The cooler itself still needs to be functioning correctly and that is what this violation is for. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days to ensure that the equipment has maintenance conducted and is functioning correctly.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple rags used for wiping counters were observed stored on the counters in the kitchen. The PIC was consulted and moved the rags back into the buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all wet rags are stored between uses in sanitizer of effective concentration to prevent the proliferation of biological pathogens.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The “Imperial” hot box on the prep line was observed heavily soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC this item should be cleaned nightly by staff. This appeared to not be happening at the time of the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain clean. The temperature inside of this was observed over 400F and biological contamination is not the concern. Pieces falling out of this equipment into the open sauces underneath was the concern and the impetus for maintaining this equipment clean at the time of the inspection. Ensure that all physical equipment is maintained clean at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) An employee shirt was observed in a container of flatbreads on the prep line. 2) A purse was observed stored on a wire shelf over consumer foods. Both locations were shown to the PIC and the items moved to correct. The flatbreads were also discarded to allay the potential concerns related contamination concerns. Ensure that all employee personal items are stored so that contamination of consumer foods is mitigated.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Multiple employees were observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review when hand washing is required with their staff and conduct oversight as needed. Ensure that hand washing is conducted each time that it is required by the code.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink across form the manager’s office was observed without soap. The PIC was shown and replaced the soap to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed soup to be hot holding in a warmer at 120F. Discussed with PIC, warmer was filled with too many soup bags. 2 soup bags were removed and placed in walk in cooler, and the remaining bags were able to be fully submerged in warmer and ran a temperature of 145F. Ensure staff is aware of equipment limits, any TCS food being hot held must be at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed cold holding station holding sauces to be at 50F. Discussed with PIC, cooler was serviced during inspection. After technician serviced cooler, cooler ran a temperature of 40F. Ensure all TCS food being cold held are kept at or below 41F, and that all cooler equipment is working up to manufactures standards.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed one of the cold holding drawers to not be keeping temperature. Steak and ribs were probed and were 51 and 48, respectively. Items were voluntarily discarded. The seal of this drawer does not appear to be sticking correctly which could be causing the higher temperatures. The other cold holding drawer on the same unit was operating correctly which lead the Inspector to believe it was the seal that is not working correctly. PIC was present and a service call will be made. Do not use this drawer until the drawer is repaired. Inspector asked PIC to put a sign on that drawer that states, “Do Not Use”. findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Raw steaks and ribs in the far left section of the coolers under the grills are observed with internal temperatures around 50F. Investigation shows that the drawer where they are stored does not fully seal to the cooler (refer to line item #47). The cooler is also indicating that it is in its defrost cycle and the facility is currently in a major rush at the time of observation. It is believed that all three situation contributed to the cooler being out of temperature and that it has only been out for a short time. The relevant items were moved to the walk in cooler to correct, where they were observed shortly after at correct temperatures.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. 

The far left bins of the coolers under the grills do not appear to fully seal to the drawers at this time. Because of this multiple sections of steak are observed out of temperature (refer to line item #22). PIC will enquirer with their maintenance company for repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands, use a paper towel to turn off the faucet and then use the same paper towel to dry their hands. In this situation, the paper towel should have been discarded and a new paper towel(s) acquired for drying. A different approach would have been for the employee to allow the water to run as they dried their hands and turn the faucet off as they discarded the towel. Education took place.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-304.11: (A) FOOD shall only contact surfaces of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned. (B) SINGLE-SERVICE/USE ARTICLES (C) LINENS.

Multiple black specks are observed in the ice next to the bar area entrance. The machine that the ice comes from is observed clean and without specks. It is currently believed that the substance fell in at the locations. More specks are observed in the bottom of the container, therefore the container is accumulating them over time. PIC instructed to clean the location regularly and ensure that it is maintained clean. Ice was removed and the container cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

Multiple quat based sanitizers are observed around the 0-100 ppm range on the inspector’s test strips. Buckets were remade to correct. At this time, it appears that the machine is metered to only provide solution at 150 ppm, which is the very bottom end of the solutions effective range. It is believed that ongoing use is deteriorating the solution quicker than the procedure for changing solution (2 hours). It is also possible that the machine needs to be ran for a time prior to dispensing solution at effective levels. In this case, train staff appropriately.

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 

No time/ temperature sheet filled out for the rice observed cooling in the walk in cooler. This is the only item observed cooling at the time of the inspection. Logs are available for use and should be used to ensure (and track) proper cooling is taking place. Rice was cooked earlier today and a sheet filled out to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

Multiple sani buckets (4 along the cook line and by the bar entrance) in the facility are observed with concentrations ranging from approximately 50 to 100 ppm Quat. Quat sanitizers are required to be at a minimum concentration of 200 ppm per the label on the bottle. The buckets are observed with time stamps indicating that they should have been changed around an hour prior to the start of the inspection. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (I) monitoring temperatures; (K) proper sanitizing;  (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD.

1)Two coolers are observed left open long enough for foods to be observed significantly out of temperature. 2) Another cooler is observed turned off while TCS foods are present. (Refer to violation 22) 3) Multiple sanitizers throughout the facility are observed out of concentration and to not to have been changed when they should have been. (Refer to violation 16). Situations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure the employees are trained effectively in their jobs.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria. 

1)CL based sanitizer in the three part sink in the bar area is observed with a concentration of 50 ppm. Package indicates that a concentration of 100 ppm is required. Sink was remade during the inspection to correct. 2) All sani buckets in the facility are observed with concentrations ranging from approximately 50 to 100 ppm Quat. Quat sanitizers are required to be at a minimum concentration of 200 ppm. Several of the buckets are observed with time stamps indicating that they should have been changed two hours prior to the start of the inspection. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Multiple items are observed out of temperature in the facility: 1) beef in the upright cooler to the right of the grills. Cooler was left open prior to being observed by the inspector and beef was observed at 44-46 degrees. The cooler was closed and foods came back into temperature quickly. Violation corrected. 2) Chicken in the breading station was observed with an internal temperature of 64F. Investigation showed the cooler to be off. TCS foods, including the chicken, were discarded during the inspection to correct. 3) Diced tomatoes in the prep cooler across from the fryers were probed at 50F. Other items in the top of the cooler are observed up to 58F. The cooler has multiple bowls, spatulas and rags in the top area that is not allowing the cooler to be closed. The diced tomatoes were discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

An of white fuzzy substance is observed on the shelves in the walk in cooler. Inspector believes the substance to be mold. Inspector discussed with the PIC and instructed to clean often enough so as to maintain clean.
